public_rationale: On October 17, 2025, database maintainer Thomas Bloom said GPT-5 had found references to existing solutions that he had not known about [e1]. The Decoder's October 18 report documents how the announcements suggested that GPT-5 had produced new proofs, while distinguishing Kevin Weil's stronger wording from Bubeck's phrase “found solutions” [e3]. On October 20, Bubeck acknowledged confusion and explained that the work concerned existing knowledge, rather than new mathematical results [e2]. Together, these records support the claim that the announced findings were existing solutions publicly presented or understood as new discoveries [e1, e2, e3].
limitations: The evidence does not measure how many readers misunderstood or establish what every reader believed.
The evidence does not establish deliberate deception.
Weil's stronger wording cannot be attributed verbatim to Bubeck [e3].

criteria.support_condition: Records establish that the announced findings were existing solutions and that the wording was understood or publicly presented as new mathematical discoveries.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The announced findings were original resolutions of previously unsolved problems, or reliable records establish that the alleged misunderstanding did not occur.
